definitions.explanation: A person who is timid, easily frightened, or cries easily. Used as a mild insult or teasing term, especially among children.

examples.english: Don't be a crybaby! Stop crying.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}は{弱虫|よわむし}だった。
examples.english: I was a wimp when I was a kid.

examples.japanese: {弱虫|よわむし}と{呼|よ}ばれるのが{嫌|いや}で、{勇気|ゆうき}を{出|だ}して{挑戦|ちょうせん}した。
examples.english: I didn't want to be called a coward, so I mustered my courage and took on the challenge.

notes:
A compound of {弱|よわ}い (weak) and {虫|むし} (bug/insect). The {虫|むし} suffix is used in several Japanese words to describe personality types, similar to English expressions like "bookworm."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {弱虫|よわむし}な{子|こ}: a timid child
- {弱虫|よわむし}と{呼|よ}ばれる: to be called a wimp
- {弱虫|よわむし}を{克服|こくふく}する: to overcome one's timidity

RELATED WORDS WITH {虫|むし}:
- {泣|な}き{虫|むし}: crybaby (focuses specifically on crying)
- {怠|なま}け{虫|むし}: lazybones
- {本|ほん}の{虫|むし}: bookworm

USAGE:
Most commonly used by or about children. Among adults, it is playful or teasing rather than a serious insult. Can function as a な-adjective when modifying nouns: {弱虫|よわむし}な{性格|せいかく} (a timid personality).
